questions.q: Which reagent converts unactivated chlorobenzene into aniline by the elimination–addition (benzyne) route?
options: Ethanolic NH₃ in a sealed tube at 373 K
questions.explain: Only a very strong base such as NH₂⁻ can remove the ortho H and eliminate HCl to give benzyne. Ordinary ammonia does not substitute an unactivated aryl halide.

questions.q: Chlorobenzene labelled with ¹⁴C at C-1 is treated with KNH₂ in liquid NH₃. In the aniline formed, the label is found:
options: At C-1 and C-2 in equal amounts
Only at C-1, the carbon bearing NH₂
Spread equally over all six ring carbons
questions.explain: Roberts' 1953 result: NH₂⁻ adds to either end of a symmetrical benzyne, so half the aniline has NH₂ on the labelled carbon and half on its neighbour (cine substitution). Direct addition–elimination would keep the label only at C-1.

questions.q: Which aryl halide does NOT react with NaNH₂ in liquid NH₃ by the benzyne mechanism?
questions.explain: The first step needs a hydrogen ortho to the halogen. In 2-bromo-1,3-dimethylbenzene both ortho positions carry CH₃, so benzyne cannot form.

questions.q: 2-Chloroanisole is treated with NaNH₂ in liquid NH₃. The product is:
questions.explain: The benzyne has its triple bond next to –OCH₃, and NH₂⁻ adds to the farther carbon so that the aryl anion sits next to the –I oxygen. The NH₂ therefore ends up meta to OCH₃, not where the chlorine was.
